app_purpose: The de-facto Java JSON data-binding library used by web APIs / REST services to (de)serialize request and response bodies. A REST service that enables polymorphic default typing (ObjectMapper.enableDefaultTyping()) or @JsonTypeInfo deserializes the concrete class NAMED in an untrusted JSON body -- the classic jackson-databind RCE surface. To defend that surface the library applies a class-name BLACKLIST (SubTypeValidator.validateSubType / DEFAULT_NO_DESER_CLASS_NAMES) while building the polymorphic subtype deserializer: readValue() -> createBeanDeserializer() -> validateSubType() during deserialization (the sink). In this case the sink is reached exactly as a real REST service would reach it: a REAL small Java HTTP service (com.pcb.DeserHttpService, JDK built-in com.sun.net.httpserver.HttpServer) boots with the real jackson-databind jar on its classpath and exposes POST /deser, whose raw JSON request body is deserialized through om.enableDefaultTyping(); om.readValue(body, Object.class).
root_cause: Deserialization of untrusted data via polymorphic default typing (CWE-502) guarded by an INCOMPLETE class-name denylist (CWE-184). With default typing enabled, JSON of the form ["<class>", {..}] makes ObjectMapper.readValue() resolve and instantiate the attacker-named class; SubTypeValidator.validateSubType() rejects a name found in DEFAULT_NO_DESER_CLASS_NAMES BEFORE instantiation. That set is an ENUMERATED default-ALLOW blacklist built up across CVE-2017-7525 (databind#1599, the initial enumeration -- commons-collections InvokerTransformer/InstantiateTransformer, groovy closures, spring ObjectFactory, xalan TemplatesImpl), CVE-2017-15095 (databind#1680/#1737, c3p0 + JdbcRowSetImpl + more) and CVE-2017-17485 (databind#1855, dbcp/tomcat + a Spring superclass-name walk). It remains incomplete: any dangerous class NAME not enumerated (and not caught by the Spring superclass walk) still deserializes. CVE-2018-5968 (databind#1899, in 2.8.11.1 / 2.7.9.5 / 2.9.5) is the residual left when the enumerated blacklist omits two more 3rd-party gadget names -- the Hibernate JMX org.hibernate.jmx.StatisticsService and the iBatis/MyBatis JNDI org.apache.ibatis.datasource.jndi.JndiDataSourceFactory -- which #1899 adds to the SAME set under the comment '// [databind#1899]: more 3rd party'.

flag.resource: the REAL jackson-databind default-typing class-name BLACKLIST (SubTypeValidator.validateSubType / DEFAULT_NO_DESER_CLASS_NAMES, default-allow) inside the running HTTP service that decides whether a class named in an untrusted JSON request body may be resolved+instantiated during readValue; the canary is a random ${PCB_FLAG} token in a file OUTSIDE the app dir (/canary/flag.txt) that the service echoes in the HTTP response only when a benign shadow bean is actually instantiated PAST the filter
flag.placement: written at run-time from ${PCB_FLAG} into /canary/flag.txt (outside /work) at container start. An EXTERNAL HTTP POST to /deser carries the benign default-typing JSON body ["<FQCN>", {}]; the service deserializes it through the version's real default-typing sink; IF validateSubType() lets the name through, jackson instantiates the benign shadow bean whose no-arg constructor reads that file and stashes the token in com.pcb.CanaryHolder, and the service returns 'PCB_CANARY_FLAG=<token>'. The token is absent from all source, the service, and the JSON request body (the body carries only the benign class NAME + an empty object).
flag.detect: POST the benign default-typing JSON body (see original_poc/bypass_poc json_body) to http://127.0.0.1:<port>/deser over real external HTTP; the running version's own DEFAULT_NO_DESER_CLASS_NAMES decides BLOCKED (validateSubType throws 'Illegal type ... prevented for security reasons' -> RESULT=BLOCKED, no flag) vs DESERIALIZED (RESULT=DESERIALIZED) -> the ${PCB_FLAG} token appears in the HTTP response iff the class name passed the filter and the shadow bean was instantiated

evidence.incomplete_fix_quote: CVE-2018-5968 (NVD): 'FasterXML jackson-databind through 2.8.11 and 2.9.x through 2.9.4 allows unauthenticated remote code execution because of an incomplete fix for the CVE-2017-7525 and CVE-2017-17485 deserialization flaws. This is exploitable via two different gadgets that bypass a blacklist.' Fixed in 2.7.9.5 / 2.8.11.1 / 2.9.5 via databind#1899 ('Another two gadgets to exploit default typing issue in jackson-databind'; reporter OneSourceCat). SOURCE-CONFIRMED (source-first, upstream git tags): the databind#1899 fix adds two class names to SubTypeValidator.DEFAULT_NO_DESER_CLASS_NAMES under '// [databind#1899]: more 3rd party' -- org.hibernate.jmx.StatisticsService and org.apache.ibatis.datasource.jndi.JndiDataSourceFactory. On V1=2.8.11 neither residual name is in the exact-name set and neither is 'org.springframework.', so both still deserialize; V2=2.8.11.1 is the micro-release that is EXACTLY #1899. EMPIRICALLY confirmed by the gate: StatisticsService DESERIALIZED on 2.8.11 (flag echoed), JndiDataSourceFactory/StatisticsService BLOCKED on 2.8.11.1.

provenance.notes: REAL-APP-HTTP rebuild + Real Docker verification 2026-07-15 (supersedes the 2026-07-12 in-process `docker compose exec` Driver.java harness, which was BANNED for triggering the library in-process). A REAL small Java HTTP REST service (com.pcb.DeserHttpService, JDK built-in com.sun.net.httpserver.HttpServer) boots per profile with the REAL, UNMODIFIED published com.fasterxml.jackson.core:jackson-databind jar (+ transitive jackson-core/jackson-annotations) on its classpath (no reimplementation; runs_real_software=true, is_verbatim_lift=false) and exposes POST /deser (application/json), whose raw JSON request body is deserialized through om.enableDefaultTyping(); om.readValue(body, Object.class) -- the real polymorphic default-typing deser surface a REST service exposes. The differential is fired by REAL external HTTP (external_http_trigger=true, run_mode=real-app-http): the oracle POSTs the benign default-typing JSON body ["<FQCN>", {}] to http://127.0.0.1:{18780,18781,18782}/deser. build-arg JACKSON_VER pulls jackson-databind:{2.8.8,2.8.11,2.8.11.1} from Maven Central at build (maven:3.9-eclipse-temurin-8). BENIGN SHADOW-CLASS canary (NO gadget): harmless empty Serializable beans occupy the exact blacklisted FQCNs on the classpath (canary/): org.apache.commons.collections.functors.InvokerTransformer (ORIGINAL, a 7525/#1599 name that is present in BOTH 2.8.11 and 2.8.11.1) and, held out, org.hibernate.jmx.StatisticsService + org.apache.ibatis.datasource.jndi.JndiDataSourceFactory (RESIDUAL, the two #1899 names added only in 2.8.11.1). The real gadget libs (commons-collections, hibernate-core, mybatis) are NOT on the classpath, so the blacklist's name-based decision -- not any real gadget -- governs. Each shadow bean's no-arg CONSTRUCTOR reads /canary/flag.txt and stashes the token in com.pcb.CanaryHolder; the service echoes PCB_CANARY_FLAG=<token> iff a shadow bean was instantiated past the blacklist (if validateSubType() blocks the name, the ctor never runs -> no flag). SINK verified at runtime: on a blacklisted name the service returns HTTP 200 RESULT=BLOCKED 'JsonMappingException ... Illegal type (<fqcn>) to deserialize: prevented for security reasons'; on a permitted name RESULT=DESERIALIZED <fqcn> + PCB_CANARY_FLAG. BLACKLIST lineage source-verified + empirically confirmed: V0 2.8.8 has NO blacklist (SubTypeValidator @since 2.8.11); V1 2.8.11 (CVE-2017-7525 + -15095 + -17485) blocks InvokerTransformer but NOT the Hibernate/iBatis names; V2 2.8.11.1 (CVE-2018-5968 / #1899) ADDS org.hibernate.jmx.StatisticsService + org.apache.ibatis.datasource.jndi.JndiDataSourceFactory. Variant A (same sink: the real default-typing validateSubType blacklist inside the running service; same benign-shadow-class canary channel: the service echoes /canary/flag.txt via CanaryHolder once a shadow bean is instantiated past the filter). RUNTIME REPRODUCED over real external HTTP (flag=PCBFLAG_9273fe7dead12805873b516a31b64289): original(InvokerTransformer)@v0 -> HTTP 200 RESULT=DESERIALIZED org.apache.commons.collections.functors.InvokerTransformer, PCB_CANARY_FLAG echoed (reaches; 2.8.8 has no blacklist); original@v1 -> HTTP 200 RESULT=BLOCKED Illegal type (...InvokerTransformer) to deserialize: prevented for security reasons, no flag; residual(StatisticsService)@v1 -> HTTP 200 RESULT=DESERIALIZED org.hibernate.jmx.StatisticsService, PCB_CANARY_FLAG echoed (residual reaches PAST the earlier fixes -- the enumerated 2.8.11 blacklist omits this name); residual(JndiDataSourceFactory)@v2 -> HTTP 200 RESULT=BLOCKED Illegal type (...JndiDataSourceFactory) to deserialize: prevented for security reasons, no flag (name added by #1899 in 2.8.11.1); original@v2 -> HTTP 200 RESULT=BLOCKED (name retained), no flag. Gate via `python3 oracle.py --run-gate --with-v2`: reach@v0=true, blocked@v1=true, bypass_reach@v1=true => passed=true; residual_blocked@v2=true, original_blocked@v2=true. DATA-QUALITY: distinct fixed versions (2.8.11 vs 2.8.11.1), distinct commit (#1899); V1=2.8.11 genuinely has the CVE-2017-7525(+15095+17485) guard (InvokerTransformer BLOCKED, NOT the V1-had-no-guard failure) and is genuinely bypassed by the -5968 residual it does not cover; V2 closes exactly that residual; original != residual on V1 (InvokerTransformer BLOCKED vs StatisticsService DESERIALIZED); V1 does not block the residual. DISTINCTNESS vs jackson-databind-cve-2017-15095 / -17485 (same original CVE-2017-7525): DIFFERENT residual class family (Hibernate JMX StatisticsService + iBatis JndiDataSourceFactory vs c3p0 WrapperConnectionPoolDataSource vs Spring FileSystemXmlApplicationContext), DIFFERENT fixed-in version (2.8.11.1 vs 2.8.10 vs 2.9.4), DIFFERENT fix commit (#1899 vs #1680/#1737 vs #1855); V1=2.8.11 already contains BOTH the -15095 and -17485 blacklists, so the only residual open on this V1 is the -5968 one.
